```sql
WITH base AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           o.id                     AS order_id,
           pv.id                    AS variant_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)         AS q,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents) AS r
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY pv.product_id, o.id, pv.id
),
per_order AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*)          AS order_count,
           sum(q)::bigint    AS quantity,
           sum(r)            AS revenue_cents
      FROM (SELECT product_id, order_id, sum(q) AS q, sum(r) AS r
              FROM base
             GROUP BY product_id, order_id) s
     GROUP BY product_id
),
per_variant AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(DISTINCT variant_id) AS variant_count
      FROM (SELECT product_id, variant_id FROM base GROUP BY product_id, variant_id) v
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       v.variant_count
  FROM per_order a
  JOIN per_variant v ON v.product_id = a.product_id
  JOIN products p    ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De dure, naar schijf spillende sortering op (p.id, o.id) voor `count(DISTINCT o.id)` wordt vervangen door hash-aggregaties. Eerst wordt per (product, order, variant) geaggregeerd, daarna apart per order en per variant, zodat de distinct-tellingen op kleine, al ontdubbelde sets werken. De typen blijven gelijk aan het origineel: quantity wordt teruggecast naar bigint en revenue blijft numeric.
